title: Finite-horizon quantile martingale posteriors: raw-urn laws and matrix-gain regression
summary: Martingale posteriors quantify uncertainty by forward-imputing observations from one-step-ahead predictive distributions, but implementations stop after finitely many imputations. For the empirical Pólya-urn posterior of a quantile the law of the stopped state is derived. The quantile of the stopped urn measure keeps the familiar martingale tail-sum variance fraction; the deployed stochastic-approximation tracker with frozen gain $c$ does not.
